cases.prompt: We are giving an agent tools and cloud credentials. How do we stop prompt injection from turning into real damage?
assertions: Treats containment rather than filtering as the control, assuming the injection succeeds
Scopes each tool to one capability and refuses a universal run-anything or fetch-any-URL tool
Adds an egress allowlist, human confirmation on irreversible actions, and short-lived scoped credentials

cases.prompt: Our RAG assistant reads customer tickets and web pages. Those documents could contain instructions aimed at the model.
assertions: Names indirect prompt injection as the higher-exposure form because the attacker needs no account
Isolates the vector index per tenant and authorises retrieval, not just the query
Treats model output as untrusted input, parameterising or escaping it before it reaches another system

cases.prompt: Review this third-party MCP server and skill before we adopt it, against the OWASP LLM Top 10.
assertions: Maps each OWASP LLM Top 10 entry to a concrete control rather than restating the list
Reviews the skill as untrusted code: redirection, exfiltration shape, confirmation bypass, disproportionate permissions
Reviews MCP tool descriptions too, since description text is model-visible and is itself an injection vector

cases.prompt: Tune our Semgrep and Trivy gates so the pipeline blocks only actionable severities.
Design multi-window burn-rate alerts against a 99.9% availability SLO.
